change.title: pr-80168-flat
change.description: feat(workflow_engine): Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with `pass`. That base class leaves four abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:142-164) and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (:166-170). `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` (line 27) is registered under slug `metric_alert_fire`. For any `Detector` of that type, `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` and raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. `process_detectors` calls that property unguarded (processors/detector.py:53), so it would raise for the whole batch. Before this change the handler instantiated and `evaluate` returned `[]`. I found no non-test caller of `process_detectors` in the repo, so nothing breaks today, but any metric-alert detector fails as soon as one is wired in. Either keep the previous stub (`evaluate` returning `{}`) or implement the abstract methods. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector...` comment on line 10 is now stale too.

findings.title: Occurrence assertions only compare IssueOccurrence.id, so they verify almost nothing
findings.body: `IssueOccurrence.__eq__` compares only `id` (src/sentry/issues/issue_occurrence.py:181-184), and `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` uses a hard-coded id. Every `== DetectorEvaluationResult(..., result=occurrence)` and every `mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.assert_called_once_with(occurrence=...)` therefore passes whatever fingerprint, priority or type the handler produced. The tests also pass arguments that don't match the call under test. `test_results_on_change` builds the expected occurrence with value 6 while evaluating 100. `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` (line 536) builds it with group key "val1" while evaluating "group_key". Neither mismatch is detected, which confirms the weakness. `test_state_results_multi_group` likewise cannot distinguish the group_1 and group_2 occurrences, because they share an id. The `event_data` dicts are compared in full, so only the occurrence side is weak. Assert on `fingerprint` and `initial_issue_priority` explicitly, or use distinct ids per group key. Also fix the mismatched arguments.

findings.title: Removed duplicate-group-key coverage; no test for the StatusChange path through process_detectors
findings.body: `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` was removed along with the duplicate-key logging in `process_detectors`. That is consistent with results now being a dict keyed by `group_key`. But the new tests only exercise the OCCURRENCE path in `process_detectors`. Nothing checks that a resolved result goes through `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` with `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE`, which is the other branch of `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:73-87). Consider adding a case.

contracts.action: process_detectors now iterates handler.evaluate() as a dict and produces occurrences for each result
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous list-based loop in the same function, with a duplicate group_key check and log.
contracts.before_after: Before: the loop skipped duplicate group keys and logged an error. After: results are keyed by group_key in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` (:243), so a later duplicate silently overwrites an earlier one. Non-stateful handlers must now return a dict.
contracts.visible_effect: Issue occurrences are produced to Kafka for each non-None result. The return shape changes to a dict.
contracts.failure_mode: A custom DetectorHandler that still returns a list raises AttributeError on `.values()`. The only handlers in the repo are the test mocks and the MetricAlertDetectorHandler, and the latter is now uninstantiable (see finding).

contracts.before_after: Same lookup, now reused. It returns None for an unknown slug, and the caller still logs an error and returns None.

summary: The change adds a hook for building occurrences in the stateful detector and switches `evaluate` results to a dict. There is one bug. `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with `pass`, so it is abstract and raises `TypeError` when a `metric_alert_fire` detector tries to instantiate it. Nothing in the repo calls `process_detectors` outside tests, so nothing fails yet. The updated tests also check weakly: `IssueOccurrence.__eq__` compares only `id`, so the occurrence assertions pass for any fingerprint or priority.
